analysis.title: Line In The Sand: Goldman's Top Tech Specialist Flags The Most Important Level For The Market
key_insights: Goldman TMT specialist Peter Callahan's weekly note 'US TMT: what a week' says the Nasdaq 100 fell ~5% on the week, its fourth straight weekly loss. The SOX is down 28% over 22 trading days, a pace matched only a handful of times since 1997 (dot-com bust, GFC, Covid).

Callahan describes sentiment as 'a very tough market' despite strong bottoms-up data (memory pricing, compute pricing, supply/demand visibility, 3Q earnings). AI/Semis have been in a rolling bear market since summer and are about 40% off the highs.

The Nasdaq 100 is re-testing its multi-year 'base' trendline, which connects the April 2025 Liberation Day low and the March 2026 low. Thursday's close (~26,630) landed almost exactly on it. Friday's close of 26,990 is about 1% above the line and 14% below the Oct 6 record high of 31,361.

The range that held since May near 29,000 and the 200-day moving average have both given way. If the trendline breaks, the next support on Callahan's chart is the March low near 23,000, roughly 15% lower.

Flows were extreme. Thursday was the biggest put-volume day in Cboe history and Goldman's flagship basket realized vol hit 93, the highest since Liberation Day. Callahan says this 'arguably does help set the table for some technical relief' as vol normalizes.

BofA's Hartnett notes the SOX is 17% below its 200-day moving average, while good entry points since 1996 came at 20-25% below it. Morgan Stanley's Nick Savone notes Thursday's 12.2% SOX drop was the second-worst day in the index's history and left semis on a single-digit two-year forward P/E for the first time in five years.

EM Asia ex-China saw $21.7B of foreign selling in the week to Nov 6, the second-largest weekly outflow on record, mostly Taiwan and Korea. Nine of the ten largest weekly outflows on record occurred in 2026. Taiwan curbed short-selling and readied a $15B fund, and Seoul waived margin calls.

DRAM makers trade at 2-3x forward P/E (Hynix 2.2x, Samsung 2.6x, Micron 3.8x) while the DRAM spot index is up more than tenfold since late 2024 and near its record. TrendForce expects 4Q DRAM contract prices up about 20% q/q, after +40% in 3Q and +80% in 2Q.

The market is pricing a slower data center buildout in 2028 that could turn today's memory shortage into a glut. Morgan Stanley's data center team says the election probably won't affect 2027 capacity under construction, but about 5 GW of 2028 builds in Texas and Ohio are at risk of delay.

Callahan sees 'a fair bit of tension in portfolio management' since long/short semis books are hard to run when 'everything is compressed' and re-ratings have hit areas outside semis and tech. Analog semis (TXN) held up against industrials (CAT, down from about $1,060 to $559 since June) until late last week.

The S&P consumer staples valuation premium to the S&P 500 is at its highest in 10+ years, about 6 P/E points vs a long-run average of about 1. Staples trade at about 2x the 24-month forward multiple of the semiconductor index. Garrett's Delta One desk likes shorting the staples basket.

Per Goldman portfolio strategy, 80% of tech companies beat 3Q consensus by at least one standard deviation (62% for the S&P) and 2% missed. On revenue, 75% beat by at least one standard deviation and none missed by that much. Communication Services lagged, with half beating and a negative average revenue surprise.

Callahan calls it a 'day at a time' market and 'less of a benefit of the doubt market'. Client questions covered what inning we are in, non-AI durable names (ABNB, FWONK, SPHR, LYV, TTWO, DIS), software high-flyers NET and DDOG, and memory.

Upcoming catalysts: TTWO, TTD and RKLB report Monday after the close. Tuesday brings CPI (core est. +0.3% m/m), SoftBank, Infineon and Sea before the open, CoreWeave after the close, and TSMC monthly sales. Thursday brings AMAT and CSCO after the close and NBIS before the open. PPI is Friday and Nvidia reports at the end of the month.

The ZeroHedge author leans bearish on the trendline. The two prior bounces came during the capex boom, while now the Fed has cover from hot payrolls for a December hike, a newly elected Congress threatens the buildout, and AI credit is repricing. The author expects the line to be tested by Tuesday's CPI.

market_movers.rationale: Micron trades at 3.8x forward earnings while DRAM spot prices stay near records. Callahan asks whether the DRAM trio is 'interesting or risky' and calls it 'tricky, huh?'
Analog semis held up relative to industrials until the floor gave way at the end of last week.
CAT has nearly halved from about $1,060 in June to $559.

sector_views.rationale: Fundamentals and earnings remain strong, but the SOX is down 28% in 22 trading days and trades on a single-digit two-year forward P/E. Callahan says the market is hard to call and sees possible technical relief as vol normalizes.

The valuation premium to the S&P 500 is the highest in 10+ years at about 6 P/E points, and staples trade at about 2x the semiconductor index's 24-month forward multiple. Callahan expects investors to start asking which names are up too much. Delta One likes shorting the staples basket.
3Q results were best in class, with 80% beating consensus by at least one standard deviation. Price action has not followed the earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: A record put day, panic-level vol, 2x memory multiples, record Asian outflows and staples at twice the semis' multiple add up to a washout, and the trendline holds as it did in April 2025 and March 2026. Callahan says this helps set the table for technical relief.
tension_points.bear_case: The prior bounces came during the capex boom. Now the Fed has cover for a December hike, a new Congress threatens the buildout and AI credit is repricing, so the line may not survive a capex freeze and a hiking Fed together. Hartnett says SOX entry points came at 20-25% below the 200dma versus 17% now.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the multi-year trendline, about 1% below Friday's close, with next support at the March low near 23,000. Tuesday's CPI is the near-term test.

tension_points.bull_case: DRAM spot prices are near records, contract prices are still rising (+20% q/q in 4Q), and memory remains the tightest part of the AI supply chain.
tension_points.bear_case: Multiples like these imply the market sees current earnings as a peak, betting a slower 2028 data center buildout turns shortage into glut.
